first.rationale: Activation is down 6% QoQ and onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ—both are direct signals of friction in the user journey. memory_91 shows activation messaging improved week-one engagement and nudged accounts to first meaningful action, which directly addresses the activation decline. memory_86 shows onboarding shortening improved completion rates, suggesting the two declines may be related (longer/harder onboarding → lower completion → lower activation). Verifying memory_91 ensures the activation_messaging tactic remains sound and can be applied at current scale. Verifying memory_86 provides context on whether onboarding friction is compounding the activation problem. Activation_messaging is lower-risk than promotional_pricing (which could commoditize positioning against the competitor) and more directly targeted than simplify_onboarding (which requires product changes). A standard_experiment on in-product activation messaging can move the activation metric in one week while preserving the option to layer onboarding simplification if needed. This preserves long-term revenue quality by focusing on engagement and value realization rather than discounting, and it addresses the most acute metric decline.
